title: Annotatio V §.I: Lutheran vs Reformed — celestial/supernatural opposed to Capernaite, oral, or both
pass_a_gloss: For so he writes: We (Lutherans) say the mode of eating in the Supper is Heavenly and supernatural inasmuch as it is opposed to the gross Capernaite and carnal, but not to the real, True and Oral: the Reformed on the contrary oppose the heavenly and supernatural Mode of Eating not only to the gross and carnal, but also to the TRUE and ORAL.
pass_b_english: His Lutheran line: we call the Supper’s eating mode heavenly/supernatural as against gross Capernaite/carnal — not against real, True, and Oral.
He charges the Reformed with opposing that heavenly/supernatural mode not only to gross/carnal but also to TRUE and ORAL.
source_text: Ita enim scribit: Nos (Lutherani) modum manducandi in Cœna dicimus esse Cœlestem & supernaturalem, quatenus opponitur crasso Capernaitico & carnali, non autem reali, Vero & Orali: Reformati contra cælestem & supernaturalem Manducandi modum non modò crasso & carnali, sed etiam VERO & ORALI opponunt.
notes: Lutheran vs Reformed oral/true opposition charge.
